findings.title: include_website_name is missing the question mark and will never be used
findings.body: The serializer defines `def include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, while every other inclusion predicate in this file (e.g. include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?) and the ActiveModel::Serializer convention require `include_website_name?`. As a result the `website.present?` guard is dead code and `website_name` is serialized even when the user has no website, emitting `website_name: null` in the API payload instead of omitting the attribute.

findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction for TL0 users viewed anonymously
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden from anonymous viewers when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` applies (TL0 users), but the newly added `website_name` attribute is not added to that list. `website_name` is derived directly from the website URL (host, and in the same-domain case host plus full path), so anonymous visitors can still learn a TL0 user's website host/path from `website_name` even though `website` itself is suppressed, defeating the anti-spam/privacy restriction.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain branch of website_name has no test coverage
findings.body: The second branch (lines 144-146) implements distinct logic for sibling subdomains such as www.example.com versus forum.example.com, stripping the first DNS label before comparing. The new specs in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb only cover unrelated domains, identical domains, and a parent-domain website; none exercise this equal-length, >2-label branch, so a regression in the label-stripping comparison would ship undetected.

findings.title: website_name drops query string and shows a trailing slash for root URLs
findings.body: When the domains match, the method returns `website_host + URI(website).path` only. For a website such as `http://example.com/user?tab=posts` the displayed name silently loses `?tab=posts` despite the feature claiming to show the complete URL path, and for `http://example.com/` it returns `example.com/` instead of the bare host that the old client-side `website.split('/')[2]` produced.
